items.title: Aurora: Real-Time Fraud & Anomaly Detection
items.summary: A sub-15ms fraud detection pipeline processing 25,000 transactions/sec with a calibrated ensemble model, cutting chargebacks by 44%.
items.description: Aurora is a real-time risk scoring engine engineered to process high-throughput transaction streams with rigorous calibration and ultra-low latency bounds.
items.imageAlt: Aurora real-time fraud detection architecture showing latency and precision telemetry
deliverables: Calibrated gradient boosted + deep neural ensemble
highlights: Sub-15ms p99 inference latency at 25,000 events/sec
44% reduction in fraudulent chargebacks within 60 days
Zero training-serving skew through shared feature definitions
Continuous Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift detection on live transaction streams

sections.heading: The Challenge
paragraphs: Modern payment systems face adversarial fraud rings that adapt their patterns within hours. Existing batch-scoring mechanisms had a 20-minute latency window, allowing fraudulent spikes to clear before risk flags were raised.

The engineering imperative was twofold: compute real-time velocity features across sliding 5-minute and 1-hour windows, and execute an ensemble inference model within a strict 15-millisecond SLA without blocking payment checkout.

sections.heading: Streaming Feature Architecture
paragraphs: We deployed a decoupled Kafka cluster ingesting raw transaction telemetry, feeding a low-latency Redis feature store with dual-write semantics. In-memory sliding window counters compute card velocity, IP entropy, and geographic displacement in under 3 milliseconds.
By formalizing schema contracts via Protocol Buffers and employing automated regression tests, we eliminated the classic divergence between offline training features and online inference features.

sections.heading: Model Architecture & Calibration
paragraphs: The scoring engine blends a LightGBM tree ensemble for tabular feature interactions with a PyTorch temporal attention network capturing transaction sequence dynamics. Model outputs are calibrated using isotonic regression to ensure predicted risk probabilities directly correspond to empirical default rates.
Inference was optimized using NVIDIA Triton Inference Server with dynamic batching and INT8 quantization, slashing GPU memory footprint by 65% and stabilizing p99 latency at 11.8ms.

items.title: Pulse: High-Throughput Streaming Feature Store
items.summary: A distributed streaming feature store ingesting 1.8B events/day with Apache Spark & Kafka, achieving p99 retrieval latency under 4ms.
items.description: Pulse provides unified feature engineering and point-in-time correct retrieval for both batch model training and sub-second online inference.
items.imageAlt: Pulse distributed feature store architecture diagram with Spark and Kafka pipelines
deliverables: dbt data quality assertions & metadata catalog
highlights: 1.8 billion streaming events ingested and processed daily
p99 feature retrieval latency reduced to 3.8ms
Automated data contracts preventing schema drift downstream
Historical point-in-time feature extraction without data leakage

sections.heading: Unified Feature Ingestion
paragraphs: Data science teams frequently re-implement the same features in both SQL for offline training and Python microservices for online serving. Pulse provides a unified declarative feature repository where transforms are defined once and compiled into both streaming Kafka jobs and batch Spark pipelines.
The architecture ingests over 1.8 billion daily interactions, materializing real-time aggregates into an in-memory key-value tier while streaming raw Parquet files into a partitioned lakehouse.

sections.heading: Point-in-Time Correctness
paragraphs: Feature leakage is the most pervasive cause of failed ML deployments. Pulse implements an as-of join engine in PySpark that reconstructs the exact state of entity features at any historical timestamp.
Data scientists can run training dataset generation across terabytes of historical logs without risking future information contamination.

items.title: Verdant: Clinical NLP & Entity Extraction Engine
items.summary: Transformer-based token classification and entity linking across 12M+ biomedical records, achieving 96.8% macro F1 score.
items.description: Verdant parses unstructured clinical records into structured ontologies (SNOMED-CT and RxNorm) with calibrated confidence intervals.
items.imageAlt: Verdant clinical entity extraction visualization with token confidence metrics
highlights: 96.8% macro F1 score across 42 biomedical entity classes
Distributed Ray pipeline parsing 8,000 records/minute
Exact confidence calibration for medical audit compliance
Seamless integration with FHIR healthcare standards

sections.heading: Clinical Document Parsing
paragraphs: Healthcare data is predominantly stored in messy, unstructured clinical notes laden with shorthand, inconsistent formatting, and complex medical syntax. Verdant fine-tunes domain-specific Transformers to extract symptoms, medication dosages, and anatomical sites.
Extracted mentions are linked to standardized SNOMED-CT concepts through a dense vector retrieval index, disambiguating complex clinical terminology.

sections.heading: Distributed Inference at Scale
paragraphs: To backfill 12 million historical clinical records, we scaled the model across an elastic Ray cluster. Dynamic batching and mixed-precision inference allowed the system to process over 8,000 notes per minute.
Prediction uncertainties were calibrated using temperature scaling, routing low-confidence decisions to clinical reviewers while auto-approving 91% of extractions.

items.title: Lumen: Low-Latency Enterprise Vector Search & RAG
items.summary: Sub-30ms hybrid lexical-vector retrieval architecture over 40M enterprise documents with semantic caching and cross-encoder reranking.
items.description: Lumen combines dense vector embeddings with sparse BM25 indices to deliver accurate, hallucination-resistant retrieval for enterprise intelligence systems.
items.imageAlt: Lumen enterprise retrieval architecture and semantic vector indexing dashboard
deliverables: Cross-encoder reranking model with ONNX optimization
Semantic vector cache reducing LLM calls by 38%
Ground-truth evaluation harness with automated recall scoring
highlights: p95 retrieval latency under 28ms across 40M documents
92.4% Recall@10 on domain-specific technical queries
Semantic query caching saving $14,000/mo in inference compute
Zero-downtime rolling index updates via partitioned collections

sections.heading: Hybrid Retrieval Architecture
paragraphs: Pure vector retrieval frequently fails on exact keyword matches, code symbols, and alphanumeric model codes. Lumen deploys a hybrid retrieval architecture combining BM25 inverted indexes with dense vector embeddings.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) harmonizes sparse and dense results, passing top candidates to a lightweight cross-encoder reranker compiled with ONNX Runtime.

sections.heading: Performance & Semantic Caching
paragraphs: By implementing a semantic vector cache that matches incoming queries within a tight cosine similarity threshold, the architecture eliminates redundant retrieval queries for frequent topics.
Ray Serve manages request batching and model concurrency, maintaining stable sub-30ms latencies even during high peak query spikes.

items.title: Nomad: Supply Chain Spatio-Temporal Demand Forecasting
items.summary: Hierarchical Bayesian forecasting model coupled with distributed PySpark aggregations, predicting inventory requirements across 450 regional hubs.
items.description: Nomad models multi-scale demand fluctuations, promotional spikes, and weather anomalies across hundreds of regional distribution centers.
items.imageAlt: Nomad supply chain spatio-temporal forecasting pipeline visualization
deliverables: Automated Airflow DAG orchestrating daily forecasts
highlights: 28% reduction in inventory stockout events across 450 hubs
Daily batch pipeline processing 15M SKU-location combinations in 35 mins
Probabilistic forecasts with calibrated quantile intervals (p10, p50, p90)
Automated backtesting framework running rolling cross-validation

sections.heading: Hierarchical Time Series Forecasting
paragraphs: Forecasting SKU-level demand requires reconciling aggregate national forecasts with volatile local hub fluctuations. Nomad implements a hierarchical reconciliation framework (MinT) that guarantees mathematical consistency across all regional levels.
Models produce probabilistic quantile forecasts (p10, p50, p90), enabling inventory planners to make risk-weighted procurement decisions.

sections.heading: Scalable Spark Execution
paragraphs: Running daily forecasts across 15 million time-series combinations required fine-grained partition management in PySpark. We optimized Delta Lake z-ordering on SKU and location keys, reducing read I/O by 78%.
The batch pipeline completes in 35 minutes, providing refreshed forecasts before morning logistics shifts commence.

items.title: Atlas: Multi-Petabyte Lakehouse Migration & Query Optimizer
items.summary: Architected a modern Delta Lake storage foundation replacing legacy Hadoop clusters, reducing compute expenditure by 52% and query runtimes by 4.2x.
items.description: Atlas modernized enterprise data infrastructure into an open Lakehouse architecture with ACID transactions, automated compaction, and governance.
items.imageAlt: Atlas Lakehouse storage architecture and distributed query benchmarks
deliverables: Lakehouse migration roadmap and automated migration scripts
Federated query engine deployment with Trino
Comprehensive data observability and cost governance dashboards
highlights: 52% reduction in annual cloud compute infrastructure spend
4.2x faster average analytical query runtimes
Zero downtime migration across 3.4 Petabytes of enterprise data
ACID transactional guarantees eliminating concurrent write corruption

sections.heading: The Lakehouse Modernization
paragraphs: Legacy Hive and Hadoop clusters struggled under growing analytical workloads, causing table lock contention, silent read corruption, and massive compute costs. Atlas migrated 3.4PB of historical data to an open Delta Lake architecture.
We introduced automated file compaction, metadata vacuuming, and bloom filters that drastically reduced small-file problems and enhanced storage efficiency.

sections.heading: Query Acceleration & Cost Governance
paragraphs: We deployed Trino as the unified query engine, enabling quantitative analysts and data scientists to query petabyte-scale datasets in seconds using standard SQL. DuckDB was integrated for fast in-memory prototyping on developer laptops.
Through compute rightsizing and intelligent partition pruning, monthly infrastructure costs dropped by 52% while user query satisfaction hit all-time highs.
